q: How sensitive is the 7,643/5,078/1,213/543 pangenome partition to Roary's BLASTP identity cutoff, and which of the paper's headline Venn cells are stable vs unstable under 90-98% cutoff sweeps?
basis: The paper (and this replication) uses Roary's default 95% BLASTP identity. Our Δ≤1 gene agreement is impressive but the exact numbers are conditioned on this single hyperparameter. Without a sensitivity sweep, we cannot separate 'real biology' from 'tooling choice' in the accessory/core split.
next_steps: Rerun Roary at identity cutoffs 90/92/94/95/96/98% on the same four Prokka-annotated genomes. Tabulate pangenome, core, accessory, unique, and each Venn cell for PA34 vs the three references. Identify which cells collapse or explode across the sweep. Report a stability score per cell and re-evaluate whether '543 unique genes' is a robust biological signature or a Roary-95% artifact.

q: Can the paper's manually-derived '≥24 genomic islands' be automatically re-derived on PA34 with modern tooling (IslandViewer 4, Phaster prophage, integron finders), and what is the concordance with Subedi's manual MAUVE calls?
basis: C13 was explicitly deferred as out-of-scope in this replication because MAUVE-based GI calling is manual and subjective. This leaves a real gap: PA34's accessory-genome story leans on the GI count, but neither the paper's boundaries nor ours are automatically reproducible.
next_steps: Run IslandViewer 4 (SIGI-HMM + IslandPath-DIMOB + Islander), PHASTEST for prophages, IntegronFinder2 for integrons, and merge/dedupe. Compare the automated GI set against the paper's 24 manually-called GIs by chromosomal coordinate overlap. Report concordance %, novel GIs discovered by automation, and any 'lost' paper GIs that fall below automated thresholds.

q: Is the plasmid-borne AMR cluster on pMKPA34-1 (containing tmexCD3-TOprJ3, sul1, dfrA15, blaNPS, etc.) mobilizable in trans, and what is its transmission potential to other Pseudomonas / Enterobacteriaceae in ocular/nosocomial contexts?
basis: The paper reports six plasmid AMR genes and we recover the plasmid (95.4 kbp, GC 57.2%) exactly with 9 AMR genes on it including the recently-recognized tmexCD3-TOprJ3 efflux operon. The paper's clinical narrative depends on plasmid mobility but neither work directly interrogates transfer machinery or host range.
next_steps: Analyze pMKPA34-1 for conjugation systems (T4SS/TrbBC, oriT prediction via oriTfinder, relaxase identification), plasmid-typing (PlasmidFinder inc groups, MOB-suite), and mash-screen against public plasmid databases (e.g. NCBI RefSeq plasmids) to find close cognates and infer host range. Report whether tmexCD3-TOprJ3 mobilization risk is genuine and identify sister plasmids in ocular / eye-hospital surveillance data if available.

q: Of PA34's 543 'unique' genes (present in no other of the 3 references), how many encode products with plausible function (validated HMM hits, structural predictions, essentiality signals) vs how many are annotation noise, paralogs miscalled as unique, or fragments of mobile elements?
basis: The '543 unique genes' is one of the paper's headline claims and reproduces exactly here — but 'unique in Roary output' is a computational category, not a biological one. Prokka + Roary at 95% ID can inflate uniqueness via short/fragmentary calls, paralog splits, or IS-element pieces.
next_steps: For each of the 543 unique genes: (a) hmmscan vs Pfam-A + TIGRFAM to test for known-domain content, (b) run against ISFinder to flag IS-element fragments, (c) BLAST against the full nr Pseudomonas set to catch strain-specific paralogs Roary missed, (d) AlphaFold3/ESMFold structural prediction on sequences with no domain hits. Classify each gene as functional-orphan, mobile-element-fragment, paralog-artifact, or unknown. Report the fraction that is biologically real vs computational.

q: Are the 124 orthologs shared exclusively between the two eye-isolate strains (PA34 and VRFPA04) a genuine ocular-niche adaptation signature, or an artifact of the small 4-strain comparison set that would dissolve under a broader P. aeruginosa pangenome?
basis: The paper (and this replication) highlights 124 exclusive PA34∩VRFPA04 orthologs as evidence of shared ocular adaptation. But with only 4 strains, any two-strain intersection is over-represented. The 124 could shrink dramatically when comparing PA34 against 100+ non-eye Pseudomonas.
next_steps: Extend the pangenome to ~100 P. aeruginosa strains (mix of clinical, environmental, eye, non-eye) using PPanGGOLiN or a scalable Roary variant. Recompute PA34∩VRFPA04 exclusive orthologs against this broader background. If the count remains substantial and enriched for functions plausible for corneal colonization (e.g. iron acquisition on eye surface, lipid metabolism for tear film, biofilm on lens epithelia), that supports the ocular-niche hypothesis; if it collapses to <10, treat the 124 as small-comparison-set artifact.
